head: 7d048b47296b9e34ed76ed2fd55be16587eb12a6
scope: Issues 185, 193, and 194. A foreground lane router on port 18797 ran this code on Linux 7.0 x86_64, with its state on the machine's ext4 disk. It used the real accounts through copies of the dobby and work logins (lane.py, lane-config.json). The daily router kept running beside the lane, unchanged. A real claude -p request for claude-haiku-5-5 started a conversation. A lane restart over an events.jsonl that ended in a newline added no blank line. lane.py then stopped the lane and appended the first half of the last event line, as a short write leaves it. After the next restart, the first new event, model_catalog, began on a line of its own and parsed. A resume of the first conversation stayed on its account and kept its content, and digest.go's readDigest and account.go's requestsSince counted its request. The helper changes, the platform note text and the removed activate --agent-sdk flag, send no request; tests/test_claude_router_activate.py covers them. record.py built the record. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun.

matrix.scenario: dobby token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
work token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code and executable match the build at 7d048b4
Both lane accounts are signed in with paid overflow disabled at start
The lane read the model catalog and serves claude-haiku-5-5
A new conversation for claude-haiku-5-5 is placed and answered through the lane
A restart over an events.jsonl that ends in a newline adds no blank line
Before the restart, events.jsonl ends mid-line with the first half of its last event
After the restart, the first new event starts on a line of its own and parses
After the restart, resuming the first conversation stays on its account and keeps its content
digest.go and account.go read the events after the restart, including the first new event's line

detail.method: lane_readers_test.go, added only to a temporary copy of the checkout, called readDigest (digest.go) and requestsSince (account.go) on the lane's events.jsonl after the restart, with the restart time as the window start. It decoded the first line after the partial line into claude.Event, the type both readers decode.

matrix.scenario: claude-router cache reads the lane's events.jsonl after the restart
Identity is the same at the start and the end

detail.method: lane.py hashed each refresh token in the daily login before it copied it, and again in the lane's copy after the last stop. It then deleted the copies. events.jsonl holds no credential_refresh event.

matrix.scenario: Evidence contains no copied access token

detail.method: Exact client token and the tokens in the lane's login copies, plus sk-ant-, JWT, and Bearer patterns, before the copies were deleted.
detail.rescan: A second scan covered every evidence file and accepted.json. rescan.json lists its files, method, and hits.

incidents.finding: lane.py expected the first event after a start to be started, but the service writes model_catalog first, then the overage reads, then started. The three rows that named started failed. The router met their intent: after the restart over the partial line, the next byte was a newline and the first new line, model_catalog, parsed.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py: those rows check that the first new line parses and record its kind

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code

offline_verification.head: 7d048b47296b9e34ed76ed2fd55be16587eb12a6
offline_verification.tmpdir: ext4, under the lane directory, so the journal tests, including the kill -9 test, ran on the machine's own disk
